samples.summary: The slides numeric band exists only on the REST PUT; the collaborative Yorkie read path applies none, so a peer bypasses the new gate for the exact threat it documents
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the `fontSize` band in `normalizeSlideInlines` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1027, 1060, 1206) are reachable only from `assertValidSlidesBody`, which the diff's own JSDoc calls "the *only* boundary that can do it" because a slide text body "is persisted verbatim as JSON by `writeSlidesRoot` and read back verbatim — it passes through no codec at all". That premise is what makes the gate bypassable: the normal editing channel is a direct Yorkie write, not the REST endpoint. `hydrateRoot` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:283-297) is the only thing that inspects a stored deck on read and does structural repair only (`if (!Array.isArray(blocks)) el.data = { blocks: [] }` at :291-293); no `normalizeFontSize`, `normalizeListLevel`, `normalizeRowHeight`, `normalizeTableSpan` or `parseColumnWidthsAttr` is imported anywhere under packages/slides/src or in the slides store (grep returns only export/pptx/text.ts). Attack: an editor on a shared deck runs a patched client and writes `elements[i].data.blocks[0].inlines[0].style.fontSize = 1e9` — or a docs `tableData` block with 100k `columnWidths` entries — into the deck; every other viewer reads it back through `yorkieToPlain` unfiltered into the shared `computeLayout`/`computeTableLayout`. The added gate covers only API callers, so the hostile-collaborator threat the change states is unmitigated for decks while reading as covered.

samples.summary: The new slides band covers fontSize but not the inline image size, the other untrusted number in a slide body that becomes a line height
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` now bands `style.fontSize` (docs-content.controller.ts:1206) on the reasoning that "a run's font size becomes its line's height, and nothing downstream of here bands it for a deck". The identical statement holds for `style.image`: packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:726-732 reads `seg.image.width`/`seg.image.height` directly as the display size and therefore the line height, and every other boundary in this change applies `isPaintableImageSize` to that pair (crdt-tree.ts parseInlineStyle, yorkie-doc-store.ts parseInlineStyle, clipboard.ts sanitizeImageData). The slides arm does not — grep for `image` in the controller returns only comments (lines 749, 1148), no validation. A `PUT /content` carrying `inlines[0].style.image = {src:'x', width: 1e9, height: 1e9}` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and reaches the shared docs layout for every viewer of the deck and the PDF/PPTX export path — the same stored-poison class the surrounding bands exist to stop, through the field the walk skipped.
searchedFor: grep isPaintableImageSize across repo (crdt-tree, yorkie-doc-store, clipboard)

samples.summary: parseColumnWidthsAttr splits the entire attribute before applying MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS, so the allocation bound its JSDoc promises is not enforced
samples.evidence: The JSDoc says the count is bounded because "a `cols` string of a million entries is a million allocations *per row*, from an attribute a peer can write. Entries past `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` are dropped." The implementation at numeric-attrs.ts:226 is `for (const part of attr.split(','))` — `split` materializes the whole array (one string per entry) before the loop's `if (widths.length >= MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS) break` can run. A peer writing a multi-megabyte `cols` Tree attribute therefore still forces a multi-million-element string array on every reader at every parse of that block; both read boundaries call this (crdt-tree.ts treeNodeToBlock, yorkie-doc-store.ts treeNodeToBlock). Bounding before the split (slice the string, or scan by index) would make the guard match its claim.

samples.summary: MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN bounds fragments per row, not per document, so many poisoned rows still multiply the page/PageLine allocation
samples.evidence: The bound is per row: `fragments` is initialised inside the per-row block (pagination.ts:152) and checked at :178. The band on the user-specified height caps one row at MAX_ROW_HEIGHT (10000 px ≈ 12 pages), but a content-derived height is capped only by this loop bound, so a document a peer writes with e.g. 500 table rows each exceeding 200 pages of content yields ~100k pages, each allocating its `PageLine` entries, on every reader's first render. The design note reasons about a single row ("no single row can hang the tab"), which is accurate but leaves the aggregate unbounded; a document-level page or fragment budget would close the residual.

samples.summary: The slides PPTX importer is an unbanded producer into the codec-free slides store — the mirror of the DOCX importer gap this change closed
samples.evidence: This change fixed the docs-side equivalent: `docx-style-map.ts` now runs `normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` on `w:sz` and `w:line` because "a producer that writes past a reader's band is the same divergence the bands exist to close, arriving from the other side". The slides PPTX importer did not get the same treatment: packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:521 writes `style.fontSize = (sz / 100) * fontScale` straight from the file's `<a:rPr sz>` with no bound (a crafted `sz="999999999"` is ~1e7 pt), and :268/:314 write `block.listLevel = attrInt(pPr,'lvl') ?? 0` unclamped. The imported body is stored on the slides path, which by this change's own premise has no read-side codec, so the value is served to every collaborator on the deck and to the export paths. The input is an uploaded, attacker-controlled .pptx — a file-parsing trust boundary, not just a peer one.

samples.summary: sanitizeDocStyles deliberately passes unrecognised keys of attacker-controlled JSON through, including a JSON-parsed `__proto__` own property
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` starts from `const styles = { ...source }` over `JSON.parse(root.stylesJson)` — a peer-writable LWW string — and documents that "a key no `StyleId` names is passed through untouched". I could not build a pollution chain today: `JSON.parse` creates `__proto__` as an own data property and object spread copies it as an own property rather than invoking the setter, and every consumer I read merges with spreads and looks entries up by fixed `StyleId` (named-styles.ts:388-403). Flagged only because this is the sanitizer for an untrusted blob and explicitly preserves arbitrary keys, so a future consumer merging the registry via `target[k] = src[k]` or `Object.assign` over `Object.keys` turns it into prototype pollution. Skipping `__proto__`/`constructor` keys costs nothing and removes the class.
searchedFor: read sanitizeDocStyles, resolveStyleInline, resolveStyleBlock in packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts
grep stylesJson producers and consumers across repo
checked docsTreeToDocument and YorkieDocStore.readDocStyles parse sites

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. The numeric bands (bandSlideBlockNumerics :1027, bandSlideCellNumerics :1060, the fontSize band in normalizeSlideInlines :1206) are reachable only via assertValidSlideBlocks (:1113-1134) -> assertValidSlidesBody (:529) -> the REST PUT at :195; all other references are specs. The premise is independently confirmed: slides bodies are plain JSON on the Yorkie root with no attribute codec (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:4-5, readSlidesRoot :52-80), unlike docs, which band at both CRDT read boundaries (docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:86, frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:203). I searched wide for a read-path counterexample and found none: no band symbol or band constant is imported anywhere in packages/slides/src or packages/frontend/src except the UI picker ceiling (font-catalog.ts:86); the one normalize call on the slides render path, normalizeBlockStyle (text-renderer.ts:265), is only default-filling (docs/src/model/types.ts:382-384); docs layout.ts reads style.fontSize raw at :124/:1059 with no clamp anywhere in the file; migrateDocument/migrateMeta (slides/src/model/migrate.ts) band only pxPerPt/slideHeight/guide position/recentColors; hydrateRoot (yorkie-slides-store.ts:283-297) is structural repair only; slides' own computeTableLayout (slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:82-92) caps neither column count nor magnitude. So an editing peer writing fontSize/rowSpan/columnWidths out of band directly into the Yorkie deck reaches every other viewer's computeLayout/computeTableLayout unfiltered, bypassing the gate that reads as covering this threat. In-lane as unguarded untrusted-peer input reaching a shared sink and as a guard bypassable at another entry point; impact is availability/render corruption for all co-viewers, consistent with major.

finding.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` now bands `style.fontSize` (docs-content.controller.ts:1206) on the reasoning that "a run's font size becomes its line's height, and nothing downstream of here bands it for a deck". The identical statement holds for `style.image`: packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:726-732 reads `seg.image.width`/`seg.image.height` directly as the display size and therefore the line height, and every other boundary in this change applies `isPaintableImageSize` to that pair (crdt-tree.ts parseInlineStyle, yorkie-doc-store.ts parseInlineStyle, clipboard.ts sanitizeImageData). The slides arm does not — grep for `image` in the controller returns only comments (lines 749, 1148), no validation. A `PUT /content` carrying `inlines[0].style.image = {src:'x', width: 1e9, height: 1e9}` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and reaches the shared docs layout for every viewer of the deck and the PDF/PPTX export path — the same stored-poison class the surrounding bands exist to stop, through the field the walk skipped.
searchedFor: grep isPaintableImageSize across repo (crdt-tree, yorkie-doc-store, clipboard)

verdict.reason: The absence itself is factually real — I confirmed no image-size band exists anywhere on the slides write or read path: normalizeSlideInlines bands only fontSize (docs-content.controller.ts:1203-1208), bandSlideBlockNumerics/bandSlideCellNumerics cover lineHeight/listLevel/rowHeights/columnWidths/padding/spans only (1027-1077), writeSlidesRoot persists verbatim JSON (yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93), and packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:910-921 and 726-733 read seg.image.width/height straight through into the line height (880-881). isPaintableImageSize is reachable only from crdt-tree.ts:100, yorkie-doc-store.ts:220 and clipboard.ts:132, none of which a slide body traverses. So no counterexample exists. However, it is out of scope for the Security lens: the endpoint sits behind CombinedAuthGuard + WorkspaceScopeGuard + ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard (docs-content.controller.ts:98) and PUT is a documented destructive full replace (162-253), so the only actor who can store the oversized pair is a principal already authorized to write arbitrary content into that same deck. There is no authorization bypass or IDOR (the poison never crosses a document/tenant boundary the writer did not already own), no secret exposure, no injection into any interpreter (the value remains a JSON number used as a layout dimension), and no crypto/SSRF/deserialization/path-traversal vector. The impact claimed — degraded or hung rendering for viewers of a deck the attacker can already fill with anything — is an input-banding/robustness consistency gap, i.e. the correctness lens's lane, where the same item is already filed (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:12). Not blocking under this rubric.

searchedFor: read docs-content.controller.ts assertValidDocsBody for a `styles` validator
finding.summary: The new `MAX_FONT_SIZE` / `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT` bands are fully bypassable through the unvalidated, peer-writable `stylesJson` named-style registry, which reaches the identical line-height sink
finding.evidence:
`docsTreeToDocument` does a bare `JSON.parse(opts.stylesJson)` into `doc.styles` with no schema validation (crdt-tree.ts:309-315). `resolveStyleBlock` then spreads that object verbatim (`named-styles.ts:284`), `effectiveBlockSpacing` uses `styleBlock?.lineHeight` raw (`named-styles.ts:639-641`), and `resolveBlockInlines` merges the registry's `inline.fontSize` as the base layer of EVERY run (`layout.ts:165-172`), which `getLineMaxFontSizePx` turns into the line height (`layout.ts:1056-1075`, `assignLineHeights` at 874-888).

Attack: a collaborator (or an API key with write scope) sets `stylesJson` to `{"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9},"block":{"lineHeight":1e9}}}`. `normalizeFontSize` (ceiling 400) and `normalizeLineHeight` (ceiling 20) are never consulted on this path, so every reader lays every paragraph out at a ~1e9 px line height — the exact million-page/row-height amplification the diff exists to prevent, now only partially absorbed by `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` (200 pages *per table row*). Non-numeric values are worse: `Math.max(1, "abc")` is `NaN` (named-styles.ts:874), giving `NaN` line heights and a blank document for every reader — the harm the diff cites as its justification for `computeTableLayout` step 5d.

The REST arm is reachable too: `assertValidDocsBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:295-316) validates `blocks`/`header`/`footer` and never inspects `styles`, and `writeDocsRoot` stores it verbatim (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:350`). A finite `1e9` survives `JSON.stringify` intact, so a single authenticated `PUT` poisons the document for every subsequent reader.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `stylesJson` is parsed with no validation and therefore bypasses MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_LINE_HEIGHT. The repository contradicts this at every read boundary. `crdt-tree.ts:329` reads `doc.styles = sanitizeDocStyles(JSON.parse(opts.stylesJson))` (import at crdt-tree.ts:49), not a bare parse. `sanitizeDocStyles` (named-styles.ts:190) routes each known StyleId entry through `sanitizeRegistryInline` (named-styles.ts:137: `normalizeFontSize(finiteOrUndefined(inline.fontSize))`) and `sanitizeRegistryBlock` (named-styles.ts:155: `normalizeLineHeight(finiteOrUndefined(block.lineHeight))`), deleting the key when the result is undefined. `numeric-attrs.ts:111-137` shows those helpers clamp to MAX_FONT_SIZE=4000 and MAX_LINE_HEIGHT=132 and drop non-finite/<=0 values, so the finding's exact payload {"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9},"block":{"lineHeight":1e9}}} becomes 4000/132, and non-numeric values are removed by finiteOrUndefined (named-styles.ts:120-122) before any NaN arithmetic. The other reader paths reach the same sanitizer: the live frontend CRDT read at yorkie-doc-store.ts:711, the history snapshot read via docsTreeToDocument at snapshot-adapters.ts:166-168, and the backend read at docs-tree.ts:250-252. The verbatim write at docs-tree.ts:350 therefore cannot deliver an out-of-band value to layout, because every consumer re-bands on read. The absence claim is false.

searchedFor: grep rowSpan|colSpan in packages/docs/src/model and view
finding.summary: `rowSpan` / `colSpan` are still read through a bare `Number(...)` at both hardened boundaries and drive an unbounded fixed-point loop — a peer-written `rowSpan="Infinity"` hangs the tab of anyone who selects cells in that table
finding.evidence:
Both read boundaries the change hardened leave the spans raw: `crdt-tree.ts:187-188` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:452-453` (`colSpan: attrs.colSpan ? Number(attrs.colSpan) : undefined`). `normalizeTableMerges` — the only clamp for out-of-grid spans — runs solely in the paste sanitizer (`clipboard.ts:351`) and the table-insert paths (`text-editor.ts:4440,4472`), never on the CRDT read path (verified by grep).

Sink: `expandCellRangeForMerges` (`packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:66-91`) grows the rect from the span with no clamp to the table's real dimensions — `const r2 = r + rspan - 1; if (r2 > rowEnd) { rowEnd = r2; changed = true; }` (lines 77-80). With `rspan = Infinity`, `rowEnd` becomes `Infinity` and `for (let r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++)` never terminates: a permanent main-thread hang. A large finite span (`1e9`) freezes for tens of seconds instead. It is reached from ordinary gestures — drag/shift-arrow cell selection (`text-editor.ts:2339,2359,3296`), `table-merge-context.ts:53` — and from `normalizeCellRange` (`selection.ts:112`), which runs on every render of a range that has a `tableCellRange`, so once the selection exists the hang recurs on each repaint. Same threat model, same two boundaries, no band.

verdict.reason: The finding claims both CRDT read boundaries read rowSpan/colSpan through a bare Number(...) with no band, letting a peer-written "Infinity" span make expandCellRangeForMerges' fixed-point loop non-terminating. Both cited boundaries actually pass spans through normalizeTableSpan: packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:195-196 (import at :46) and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:460-461 (import at :55). The reviewer's quoted line numbers (crdt-tree.ts:187-188, yorkie-doc-store.ts:452-453) point at the empty-paragraph/blocks fallback objects, not the span reads. normalizeTableSpan (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:193-199) drops non-finite and negative values (so "Infinity" -> undefined -> read as 1) and clamps finite values to MAX_TABLE_SPAN = 1000 (numeric-attrs.ts:88), truncating to an integer. Tests confirm the behavior end-to-end: numeric-attrs.test.ts:255 (Infinity -> undefined), :257 (1e9 -> 1000), :284 (cell read of rowSpan '1e9' -> MAX_TABLE_SPAN). With spans bounded to finite integers <= 1000, the sink at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:77-80 can only extend rowEnd/colEnd by a bounded amount, so the while(changed) loop and the inner for loops terminate; normalizeCellRange (selection.ts:112) inherits the same bound on every repaint. The REST write path applies the same clamp at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1073. The guard the finding says is missing exists at exactly the two boundaries it names.

searchedFor: read clipboard.ts sanitizeTableData (paste path derives cols from real cells)
finding.summary: The table `cols` attribute is unbanded at the same read boundary: unbounded column count drives an O(rows × cols) allocation loop, and `Infinity`/mixed-sign ratios produce the same NaN geometry step 5d was added to prevent — but 5d covers row heights only
finding.evidence:
`const cols = (attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))` (crdt-tree.ts:209-212; identical in `yorkie-doc-store.ts` around line 466) accepts any count and any magnitude — `Number('1e400')` is `Infinity`, which passes `!isNaN`.

(a) Amplification: `numCols = columnWidths.length` drives `computeTableLayout`'s nested `for r < numRows / for c < numCols` loop, allocating a `LayoutTableCell` (plus a default line array) per iteration (`table-layout.ts:170-201`) regardless of how many cells the row actually has. A single ~2 MB `cols` attribute (1e6 entries) plus a few dozen rows is tens of millions of allocations — an OOM/freeze for every reader from one cheap write.

(b) Poisoned geometry: `columnPixelWidths = columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (table-layout.ts:157) yields `Infinity`, and a `cols="1e400,-1e400"` spanned cell makes `cellWidth` `NaN` (line 187) → `totalWidth`/`columnXOffsets` NaN → the table draws nothing. The change added step 5d specifically because "a NaN row height … blanks the table for every reader" (table-layout.ts:303-322) but published no equivalent guarantee for `columnPixelWidths` / `totalWidth`, which the renderers, hit-tests and selection math read just as raw.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing band exists. `parseColumnWidthsAttr` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:223-233) bounds the column *count* by breaking at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256` (line 91), and `normalizeColumnRatio` (lines 243-249) bounds *magnitude*: it drops any non-finite value — so `Number('1e400') === Infinity` is rejected, not passed by `!isNaN` as the finding claims — and clamps finite values into `[0, MAX_COLUMN_RATIO=1000]` (line 102), with the `Math.max(0, raw)` floor eliminating the mixed-sign `NaN` offset case. Both read boundaries the finding names call this helper: crdt-tree.ts:222 (import at :47-48) and yorkie-doc-store.ts:480 (import at :56). The reviewer's quoted `split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))` is not present at either location; a repo-wide grep for `.cols` found no other open-coded parse of the docs table `cols` attribute. So neither (a) the O(rows × cols) allocation amplification nor (b) the Infinity/NaN geometry poisoning is reachable from the attribute.
